question.prompt: For how many positive integers \(m\) does there exist at least one positive integer \(n\) such that \(m \cdot n \le m + n?\)

solutions.explanation:
For each \(m\), only one suitable positive integer \(n\) is needed. Choose the smallest allowed value, \(n=1\). Then the inequality becomes
\[
m\cdot1\le m+1,
\]
which is true for every positive integer \(m\).

Thus every positive integer \(m\) qualifies. Since the positive integers form an infinite set, there are \(\boxed{\text{infinitely many}}\) such values, choice E.
solutions.title: Choose a value that always works
